idea: Internal knowledge base and RAG system build for professional firms
pain: Twenty years of documents nobody can search
v1: A working knowledge system for one firm
verdict: Good fees and clear pain, but it is a software delivery business she would subcontract.

why.distribution: Warm across both professions; the pain is universally recognised.
why.demand: Firms are commissioning these builds now.
why.fmf: She understands the workflow but this is production software with security and support obligations.
why.revenue_structure: Build plus a hosting and maintenance fee that does recur.
why.defensibility: A crowded delivery market with platforms absorbing the middle.
why.leverage: Bespoke per firm, with patterns rather than code transferring.
why.capital: Contracted engineering and infrastructure before payment: £30-100k across multiple builds.
why.ceiling: £30k x 9 builds = £270k gross, less heavy subcontract cost.

ceiling_arithmetic: £30k x 9 builds = £270k gross, less ~45% to engineers and infrastructure = £148k net. The subcontract deduction plus the delivery risk is what keeps this off target.
carries: Clear, universally felt pain with real budget behind it.
kills: She would be running a software delivery firm without being a software engineer - margin leaves, risk stays.
test: Ask three managing partners what they have tried and what it cost.
test_pass: One offers to pay for a scoped pilot.
test_fail: They have an IT partner or a Microsoft rollout underway.
